fieldValues.title: A tracking pointer citing a closed issue is not itself detectable without a network call, and validate-all is deliberately network-free
fieldValues.summary: #591's actual defect (a grandfather citing #297, closed three weeks before the entry was next touched) cannot be caught by any local, offline check — knowing whether a cited issue is open or closed requires calling the GitHub API, which check-rfc-integration.mjs and every sibling check deliberately do not do (validate.yml runs validate-all with no network, no credentials). The disposition schema (#590, applied here to integration-allowlist.json) is not a live-staleness detector; it only stops a settled, expected closure from misreading as a regression. A pending entry whose issue quietly closes is still only caught by a human or agent re-auditing the file, not by CI.
evidence: check-publication-reachability.mjs's own comment (added by #590): "This guard cannot check GitHub issue state itself — validate-all is deliberately dependency-free and network-free (validate.yml)"

#591's own text floated an 'optional guard' that would 'assert its cited issues are open' — read literally that requires live GitHub state, which #590's precedent shows the repo has deliberately chosen not to build
No script under scripts/ makes an authenticated call to api.github.com; scripts/fetch-pinned-srs.mjs only fetches release artifacts, never issue state
